scope: Selected primary sources and supplied secondary AI outputs used to develop the GraphOS architecture. The pasted ChatGPT output was reviewed, but it does not contain the reportedly 117-source bibliography; no exhaustive review of those sources is claimed.
accessed_definition: True means relevant source content was inspected in this research session. False means the substantive conversation or repository content could not be inspected, even if a wrapper or error page was returned.

sources.title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
sources.supported_claim: A controlled comparison of 260 configurations across six benchmarks found that architecture benefits depend on baseline capability and task structure. Strong single-agent baselines often reduced the value of additional agents.
sources.limitation: The approximately 45% capability threshold is an empirical selection rule, not a universal law. Architecture-selection results concern held-out configurations within studied domains. The publisher page redirected to an inaccessible identity endpoint; the official MIT-hosted paper was inspected instead.

sources.title: When do AI agents benefit from collaboration?
sources.supported_claim: The updated project summary explains that coordination gains vary by domain and that reported error amplification measures additional execution work, not final-answer error probability.
sources.limitation: This summarizes the Nature study rather than supplying independent evidence. Older summaries describe an earlier 180-configuration, four-benchmark version.

sources.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
sources.supported_claim: The revised preprint compares five architectures across six benchmarks with standardized tools, prompts, and compute; collaboration can help decomposable work and hinder sequential planning.
sources.limitation: This is an earlier version of the same research as the Nature article, not an independent replication. Prefer the journal paper's qualified conclusions.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.supported_claim: Routing, parallelization, orchestrator-worker delegation, and evaluator-optimizer loops suit different task structures; additional complexity should earn its cost.
sources.limitation: Foundational engineering guidance rather than a universal comparative benchmark. The current page notes that tooling has changed and links to newer Managed Agents material.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.supported_claim: Parallel workers with separate contexts improved Anthropic's internal breadth-first research evaluation. Explicit delegation boundaries and effort limits reduced duplicated work and excessive exploration.
sources.limitation: Reported improvements and token multipliers are specific to the described research system and baselines; they do not establish general coding superiority or equal-cost gains.

sources.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
sources.supported_claim: Separating durable session records, replaceable agent harnesses, and execution sandboxes supports independent recovery and evolution. Credentials can be kept outside generated-code sandboxes.
sources.limitation: Describes Anthropic's implementation and observations; it does not prove that adopting these interfaces guarantees correctness or security in another system.

sources.title: Harness design for long-running application development
sources.supported_claim: Planner, generator, and evaluator roles improved demonstrated application builds. Some scaffolding became unnecessary as model capability improved; separate evaluation still detected missing interactions and stubbed features.
sources.limitation: Illustrative experiments with subjective assessment and acknowledged remaining defects; no universal performance guarantee. Components should be reevaluated through controlled ablations.

sources.title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
sources.supported_claim: A team of 16 agents produced a substantial compiler prototype through prolonged execution, task coordination, and carefully engineered tests and feedback.
sources.limitation: The author reports significant cost and remaining compiler, optimization, and code-quality limitations. Project size is not evidence of production readiness or superiority over expert teams.

sources.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
sources.supported_claim: MAST identifies 14 failure modes grouped into system design, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification, using a dataset of more than 1,600 traces across seven frameworks.
sources.limitation: A failure taxonomy and diagnostic dataset do not establish that any proposed mitigation eliminates those failures. Results depend on sampled systems, models, and tasks.

sources.title: Where Do Multi-Agent Systems Fail? Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Collective Mechanisms
sources.supported_claim: Correct final outputs can coexist with broken coordination mechanisms. Diagnostic contracts distinguish supported violations, ruled-out violations, and insufficient evidence.
sources.limitation: Recent preprint with limited transfer evidence; strong diagnostic results on one workflow did not fully generalize to another. Treat as a research direction, not established universal behavior.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.supported_claim: Evaluate actual environment outcomes with suitable code, model, and human graders. Repeated trials distinguish at-least-one-success metrics from consistency across attempts.
sources.limitation: Evaluation guidance requires task-specific implementation and judge calibration. Passing an incomplete suite does not establish complete product correctness.

sources.title: LangGraph fault tolerance
sources.supported_claim: Node retries have at-least-once execution semantics. External effects require durable idempotency identities, provider support, and reconciliation when acknowledgements are lost.
sources.limitation: Checkpointing does not provide exactly-once external effects. APIs and version requirements must be checked against the installed release.

sources.title: LangGraph checkpointers
sources.supported_claim: Synchronous durability commits checkpoints before continuing; asynchronous and exit modes trade durability for performance. Admission may need a separate durable record before graph invocation.
sources.limitation: Persistent checkpoints preserve graph state, not atomicity across arbitrary external services. Crash behavior and retention policy require application-level testing.

sources.title: LangGraph persistence
sources.supported_claim: Thread-scoped checkpointers and cross-thread stores serve different persistence purposes; in-memory checkpoint implementations do not survive process restarts.
sources.limitation: Storage mechanisms do not independently establish that saved information is correct, current, authorized, or useful for future tasks.

sources.title: LangGraph PostgreSQL checkpoint library README
sources.supported_claim: The PostgreSQL checkpoint library documents setup and use of a persistent LangGraph checkpointer.
sources.limitation: Persistent graph checkpoints do not provide end-to-end exactly-once external effects. Verify the README against the pinned dependency version. Verified by the coordinating agent during this session.

sources.title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop
sources.supported_claim: Specialized instructions and skills can remain in one agent loop when separate contexts are unnecessary; subagents should be justified by useful context boundaries and work separation.
sources.limitation: Architecture guidance rather than proof that one loop always outperforms subagents. Verified by the coordinating agent during this session.
